vetSays.line: 🍲 A person, maybe 20s, with thick glasses eats quiet by the fire, scraping the bowl clean with their thumb.
You remember the Crude bow at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
🍲 A man, maybe 40s, with grey-streaked hair is hunched over their bowl by the fire, eating like it matters.

🪤 A man, maybe 30s catches you watching the snares come off the line. "...Want to actually SEE one?" They show you — the loop, the trigger stick, where the run narrows between the roots. "Opossum trails. Check at dawn. Always." Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
🍽️ Roman weighs the day's basket against the pantry shelves and puts it down. "Enough. Carving bowls instead — we're down to the cracked ones."
the man in his 30s spent the afternoon at the workbench and made 5 Arrow — and carries them now, their own work in their own hands.

Travel 1 tile to trail edge.
— An old trail —
Where the trail crosses bare rock, someone scratched a mark — an arrow, or a tally, or a prayer. Pre-Burn. You add nothing. You remember it.

◈ FLASHBACK — Spare Socks
The flood year, three days in wet boots. Your feet went white and strange. The medic packed them with yarrow and told you: dry socks are civilization. Never again, you said.
📖 The memory leaves something behind: Yarrow — white flowers, feathery leaves. Stops bleeding. The medic taught you.
